title: Recipe 21 — Deployment and Canary (specs as versioned artifacts, pins as the only lever)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Recipe 21 treats a spec like code: stored versions, one pin per environment, promotions and rollbacks that are audit-logged, and a ramp gated on a real eval regression check.”
beats.script: Recipe 21 treats a spec like code: stored versions, one pin per environment, promotions and rollbacks that are audit-logged, and a ramp gated on a real eval regression check. [[pause:1.2s]] The editor opens 21 deployment and canary.md now. Keep this artifact in view: it is the concrete evidence behind the behavior this beat describes.

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed recipe and starters are never touched by a take.
beats.script: Live/ is scratch — the committed recipe and starters are never touched by a take. [[pause:900ms]] The driver clears live slash crewhaus.yaml in the scratch workspace now, giving this take a repeatable starting point without changing the committed example.

beats.label: Start from an empty registry
beats.cue: “The registry is file-backed under .crewhaus — scratch here, so every version and every audit record you are about to see was written by this take.”
beats.script: The registry is file-backed under .crewhaus — scratch here, so every version and every audit record you are about to see was written by this take. beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — the canary ramp evals both versions, and an eval needs a real credential.
beats.script: Sources demos/.env — the canary ramp evals both versions, and an eval needs a real credential. [[pause:1.8s]] Configured provider or platform credentials are required here, so the offline verifier checks the shape but does not execute the call. Operator-supplied demos/.env.

groups.title: Beat 1 · the spec that becomes v1

beats.label: Type recipe 01's harness
beats.cue: “Any spec will do — versioning is orthogonal to shape. Seven lines, so the interesting thing on screen is the registry, not the YAML.”
beats.script: Any spec will do — versioning is orthogonal to shape. Seven lines, so the interesting thing on screen is the registry, not the YAML. [[pause:900ms]] Watch the driver type lines 1 through 7 of starters slash cli slash crewhaus.yaml, rebuilding live slash crewhaus.yaml from a known state. The slice comes from committed source, so the fresh file exactly matches the example this take is introducing.

beats.label: Lint it
beats.cue: “Clean before it is ever stored. A registry full of specs that do not compile is worse than no registry.”
beats.script: Clean before it is ever stored. A registry full of specs that do not compile is worse than no registry. [[pause:1.5s]] The terminal is exercising the real implementation locally here, and the verifier expects a successful exit. Lint: clean — no findings.

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “GREEN with no key — and read the last two lines: compiling registered hello@v1. The registry is not a separate ritual; the compiler feeds it.”
beats.script: GREEN with no key — and read the last two lines: compiling registered hello@v1. The registry is not a separate ritual; the compiler feeds it. [[pause:1.5s]] This command is replayable offline, so its result is part of the repository's machine-checked demo contract. GREEN — assertion ok (11 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate. Also prints “registered hello@v1” — auto-registration is what puts v1 in .crewhaus/specs.

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (11 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate. Also prints “registered hello@v1” — auto-registration is what puts v1 in .crewhaus/specs

beats.label: List what the registry holds
beats.cue: “One version, and nobody typed a registry command to get it there.”
beats.script: One version, and nobody typed a registry command to get it there. [[pause:1.5s]] This is an offline proof and should complete successfully. V1.

groups.title: Beat 2 · versions, and the pins that are the aliases

beats.label: Store a second version
beats.cue: “put is the add operation. Storing a version changes nothing about what runs — that is the whole safety property.”
beats.script: Put is the add operation. Storing a version changes nothing about what runs — that is the whole safety property. [[pause:1.5s]] This is an offline proof and should complete successfully. Stored hello@v2 (190 bytes).
beats.command: crewhaus spec put hello v2 live/crewhaus.yaml

beats.label: Pin prod to v1
beats.cue: “pin is the only operation that changes what production runs. There is no separate alias map — the env pins are the aliases.”
beats.script: Pin is the only operation that changes what production runs. There is no separate alias map — the env pins are the aliases. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Pinned hello prod → v1.
beats.command: crewhaus spec pin hello prod v1

beats.label: Pin staging to v2
beats.cue: “Staging ahead of prod: the normal state of a healthy deployment.”
beats.script: Staging ahead of prod: the normal state of a healthy deployment. [[pause:1.5s]] The terminal is exercising the real implementation locally here, and the verifier expects a successful exit. Pinned hello staging → v2.
beats.command: crewhaus spec pin hello staging v2

beats.label: Resolve prod
beats.cue: “alias is the read: which version does this environment actually resolve to right now. This is the question a running daemon asks.”
beats.script: Alias is the read: which version does this environment actually resolve to right now. This is the question a running daemon asks. [[pause:1.5s]] This command is replayable offline, so its result is part of the repository's machine-checked demo contract. V1.

beats.label: Open the manifest
beats.cue: “The source of truth, on disk: the version list and the pins map. Every write to it is a tempfile-and-rename, so a concurrent promote and rollback serialize instead of interleaving.”
beats.script: The source of truth, on disk: the version list and the pins map. Every write to it is a tempfile-and-rename, so a concurrent promote and rollback serialize instead of interleaving. [[pause:1.2s]] The editor opens .crewhaus slash specs slash hello slash manifest.json now. This is the source or generated artifact behind the current step; focus on the details the first chunk called out.

beats.label: Pin tenant-a ahead of everyone
beats.cue: “A tenant on a regulatory hold, or one in an early-access beta. The overlay does not copy the spec — it points at a version everybody else already shares.”
beats.script: A tenant on a regulatory hold, or one in an early-access beta. The overlay does not copy the spec — it points at a version everybody else already shares. [[pause:1.5s]] This is an offline proof and should complete successfully. Pinned tenant=tenant-a hello prod → v2; writes the env-keyed overlay .crewhaus/specs/_tenants/tenant-a/hello.json ({"prod":"v2"}).
beats.command: crewhaus spec pin hello prod v2 --tenant tenant-a

verify.note: pinned tenant=tenant-a hello prod → v2; writes the env-keyed overlay .crewhaus/specs/_tenants/tenant-a/hello.json ({"prod":"v2"})

beats.label: Resolve prod for tenant-a
beats.cue: “v2 for tenant-a, v1 for everyone else — same environment, same vetted version set, two answers. That is the resolution order: overlay first, env pin otherwise.”
beats.script: V2 for tenant-a, v1 for everyone else — same environment, same vetted version set, two answers. That is the resolution order: overlay first, env pin otherwise. [[pause:1.5s]] This command is replayable offline, so its result is part of the repository's machine-checked demo contract. V2 — contrast with the alias-prod beat's v1.
beats.command: crewhaus spec alias hello prod --tenant tenant-a

verify.note: v2 — contrast with the alias-prod beat's v1

groups.title: Beat 4 · promote, roll back, and prove the trail

beats.label: Promote staging to prod
beats.cue: “Read the version pinned to staging, pin prod to it, audit the change. Three steps, atomic, no spec bytes copied.”
beats.script: Read the version pinned to staging, pin prod to it, audit the change. Three steps, atomic, no spec bytes copied. [[pause:1.5s]] This command is replayable offline, so its result is part of the repository's machine-checked demo contract. Promoted hello staging → prod (now pinned to v2).
beats.command: crewhaus deploy promote hello staging prod

verify.note: promoted hello staging → prod (now pinned to v2)

beats.label: Roll prod back to v1
beats.cue: “The fast lever: assert the target version exists, re-pin, audit the reason. One command, and no partial cutover survives it.”
beats.script: The fast lever: assert the target version exists, re-pin, audit the reason. One command, and no partial cutover survives it. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Rolled back hello prod → v1 (was v2).
beats.command: crewhaus deploy rollback hello prod v1

verify.note: rolled back hello prod → v1 (was v2)

beats.label: Verify the deployment audit chain
beats.cue: “Two deployment_action records, hash-chained, gapless from sequence zero, and the on-host tail anchor matching. Replay that log and you know who pinned what, when.”
beats.script: Two deployment_action records, hash-chained, gapless from sequence zero, and the on-host tail anchor matching. Replay that log and you know who pinned what, when. [[pause:1.5s]] This is an offline proof and should complete successfully. Hash chain intact — the promote and rollback records, each chained to the previous hash.

verify.note: hash chain intact — the promote and rollback records, each chained to the previous hash

groups.title: Beat 5 · migrations — the schema delta, not the behavior delta

beats.label: Migrate every spec in the registry
beats.cue: “It walks the registry, computes the chain of up steps per spec, and applies them — landing a fresh v3. Migration shaves off the schema delta; canary is for the behavior delta. The two compose, in that order.”
beats.script: It walks the registry, computes the chain of up steps per spec, and applies them — landing a fresh v3. Migration shaves off the schema delta; canary is for the behavior delta. The two compose, in that order. [[pause:1.5s]] This command is replayable offline, so its result is part of the repository's machine-checked demo contract. Migrate hello@v2 → v3 · migrated=1 skipped=0 failed=0.

verify.note: migrate hello@v2 → v3 · migrated=1 skipped=0 failed=0

beats.label: Ramp v3 against v1, gated on a regression check
beats.cue: [needs-key] “At each step it evals both versions against the same dataset and graders, then feeds the two results into the regression gate. Pass every step and prod auto-promotes; fail the first and it auto-rolls-back and stops.”
beats.script: At each step it evals both versions against the same dataset and graders, then feeds the two results into the regression gate. Pass every step and prod auto-promotes; fail the first and it auto-rolls-back and stops. [[pause:1.8s]] Configured provider or platform credentials are required here, so the offline verifier checks the shape but does not execute the call. Every ramp step runs two real evals; needs Anthropic credentials. The percentages sequence the confidence ramp — for target: cli each step evals the FULL dataset, because route() has no serving-path consumer.
beats.command: crewhaus deploy canary live/crewhaus.yaml v3 --traffic 5,25,50,100 --dataset ../../../starters/eval/.crewhaus/datasets/hello-eval/dev.jsonl --graders ../../../starters/eval/graders.yaml --from v1 --env prod --max-pass-rate-drop 0.05 --max-p95-latency-ms 5000

verify.note: every ramp step runs two real evals; needs Anthropic credentials. The percentages sequence the confidence ramp — for target: cli each step evals the FULL dataset, because route() has no serving-path consumer

groups.title: One more thing · the outcome ledger refuses to guess

beats.label: Record one outcome
beats.cue: “The ledger is the outcome path — one record per (version, outcome), from a ramp's eval samples or from your own serving boundary.”
beats.script: The ledger is the outcome path — one record per (version, outcome), from a ramp's eval samples or from your own serving boundary. [[pause:1.5s]] This is an offline proof and should complete successfully. [experiment] recorded pass for hello@v3.
beats.command: crewhaus experiment record --name hello --version v3 --outcome pass

beats.label: Ask it who won
beats.cue: “Wilson 95% intervals, and a flat refusal: n=1 is below the thirty-observation minimum. It also collapses repeat eval measurements of the same sample, because re-running a ramp does not grow the evidence.”
beats.script: Wilson 95% intervals, and a flat refusal: n=1 is below the thirty-observation minimum. It also collapses repeat eval measurements of the same sample, because re-running a ramp does not grow the evidence. [[pause:1.5s]] The terminal is exercising the real implementation locally here, and the verifier expects a successful exit. Verdict: insufficient-data — refusing to declare a winner below --min-n. Exit 0: refusing to guess is a valid answer, not a failure.

verify.note: verdict: insufficient-data — refusing to declare a winner below --min-n. Exit 0: refusing to guess is a valid answer, not a failure

beats.label: Ask for a variant assignment
beats.cue: “Exit 1, and the error is the lifecycle: no ramp wrote a split, or a ramp concluded and retired it. A surviving 50/50 file would route half your keys at a version nobody is running.”
beats.script: Exit 1, and the error is the lifecycle: no ramp wrote a split, or a ramp concluded and retired it. A surviving 50/50 file would route half your keys at a version nobody is running. [[pause:1.5s]] The refusal is the proof in this beat, so the verifier expects exit code 1. Deliberate rejection, exit 1 — no assignment exists because no --traffic-split ramp has run in this take. The message names both reasons rather than returning a default version.

verify.note: deliberate rejection, exit 1 — no assignment exists because no --traffic-split ramp has run in this take. The message names both reasons rather than returning a default version
